facts.statement: Facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy is a neuromuscular condition driven by the inappropriate activation of a gene called DUX4 in muscle tissue.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: The study found that the DUX4 protein triggers an immune response that mimics a viral infection but operates independently of the standard type I interferon pathway.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: This abnormal immune state is primarily driven by interferon-gamma signaling, which explains why inflammation in the disease does not resolve on its own.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: In experimental models of the disease, blocking interferon-gamma reduced muscle inflammation and stopped the progression of the condition.
facts.subject: animals
